newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, overnight money volatile.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, overnight money volatile.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late trading on Friday, with focus seen on the fluctuating money market, dealers said.
They said the tone on the rupiah was mixed, keeping it trading in a narrow range around the 2,370.0 level.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,369.75/70.25 at 0845 GMT against an opening of 2,372.0/73.0.

But mismatches and weekly tax payments due Friday seemed to cause overnight money to fluctuate sharply. Overnight money jumped to a high of 38 percent before it climbed down to close at 16 percent. It opened at around 14.0/15.0 percent.
One Japanese bank dealer said liquidity supply was adequate and weekly tax payments were not very large, but mismatches seemed to be the source of the roller-coaster market.
Another foreign bank dealer said a small delay in clearing results might also have caused the sudden jump.
"It fact, there is nothing serious. Some increases in the morning seemed to have made people nervous," the dealer said.
Dealers said there was no clear trend yet seen for the rupiah, but it might gain further ground on expectation of a liquidity tightening in the money market.
The strengthening of the rupiah against the dollar sparked small renewed speculation for a band widening, but many domestic operators shrugged off the thought.
One Japanese bank dealer said liquidity was the main issue for now due to the approaching Lunar New Year on February 7 and Eid al-Fitr celebrations on February 9 and 10.
Operators had placed their rupiah funds into central bank papers (SBIs) after selling dollar to Bank Indonesia last week.
"We are a bit worried over the liquidity outlook. We don't know what sort of maturity are the papers," he said.
Dealers said the central bank had also cut another 25 basis points for longer-term bilateral papers (SBIs), indicating a further move to curb offshore capital inflows.
They said offshore players had increasingly parked their funds in central bank longer-term papers on the back of interest rates easing environment in the domestic market.
The central bank cut three-, six- and 12-month money to 12.25, 12.50 and 12.75 percent, respectively.
The declining interest rates trend had also triggered rising demand for high-yielding five-year domestic bonds.
Increased interest in bonds were reflected in the latest issue of Astra International's 400 billion rupiah straight bonds at 15.5 percent which saw overwhelming response, dealers said.
Longer-term swap rates were relatively stable while overnight swaps rose sharply on tight liquidity expectation.
Overnight swaps closed at 2.5/2.5 against 0.6/0.8 at the opening. One-month swaps were at 10.50/11.25, two at 20.5/22.00, three at 32.00/34.00 and six at 71.0/72.5 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,367/2,559 and the conversion band to 2,367/2,415 on Friday, the fourth time this week after keeping it stable on Thursday.
